key_insight: PerovAgent autonomously designs ligands for halide perovskite nanocrystals while turning its search history into statistically testable chemical design principles.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide surface-capping ligand selection by optimizing binding energies and identifying validated ligand–surface interaction rules.
method: Coordinate LLM-driven reasoning with atomistic model construction and machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation.
Adaptively explore ligand chemistries on CsPbBr3 surfaces to improve the binding-energy objective.
Formulate design principles, test them prospectively, and audit for confounding.
evidence_signal: Across 10 independent campaigns, 19 of 35 principles gained prospective support, seven of those passed the confound audit, and DFT reproduced the energetic preference predicted by a recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle.
watch_item: Improved computed binding energies do not establish experimental nanocrystal performance, and many plausible principles did not survive validation.
paper_title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
